reason: Prior K-loop schedule changes passed correctness but did not promote, and noisy paired results do not show a repeatable gain. I rank the two distinct loop schedules first: interleaving pointer updates between FMOPAs has a concrete address-generation mechanism, while consuming loaded operands immediately changes reuse timing. Prefetch and scratch pitch are lower-confidence locality tests with added address or cache risk. Store-order changes have coverage and scheduling risk; grouped stores and direct ZA stores also need exact assembler support. Packing proposals could reduce or reorganize scratch traffic, but add timed work and involve more pointer and lifetime changes. The final proposal, cache_blocking, overlaps the previously reviewed 64 KiB packing idea and changes traversal and scratch lifetime, so it has the least distinct evidence.
